audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Hezekiah reform, Assyrian conquest, tribute, Jerusalem delegation, and Rabshakeh propaganda narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for centralized religious reform, bronze-serpent destruction, Philistine campaign, Samaria deportation recap, Sennacherib's conquest of Judah, temple stripping for tribute, siege delegation, multilingual propaganda, bodily humiliation threats, deceptive resettlement promises, and civilian silence.

verses.restored: In third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah became king.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.

modern.text: In the third year of the reign of Hoshea son of Elah over Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁלֹ֔שׁ לְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ חִזְקִיָּ֥ה בֶן אָחָ֖ז מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Twenty-five years old was he when he became king, and twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Abi daughter of Zechariah.

familiar.text: Twenty and five years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Abi, the daughter of Zachariah.

modern.text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ אֲבִ֖י בַּת זְכַרְיָֽה

verses.restored: He did what was right in eyes of YHWH, according to all David his father had done.

familiar.text: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that David his father did.

modern.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father David had done.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: He removed high places, broke pillars, cut down Asherah, and shattered bronze serpent Moses had made, for until those days children of Israel burned incense to it; he called it Nehushtan, a bronze thing.

familiar.text: He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.

modern.text: He removed the high places, shattered the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles. He also demolished the bronze snake called Nehushtan that Moses had made, for up to that time the Israelites had burned incense to it.

original.text: ה֣וּא הֵסִ֣יר אֶת הַבָּמ֗וֹת וְשִׁבַּר֙ אֶת הַמַּצֵּבֹ֔ת וְכָרַ֖ת אֶת הָֽאֲשֵׁרָ֑ה וְכִתַּת֩ נְחַ֨שׁ הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֗ה כִּ֣י עַד הַיָּמִ֤ים הָהֵ֨מָּה֙ הָי֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מְקַטְּרִ֣ים ל֔וֹ וַיִּקְרָא ל֖וֹ נְחֻשְׁתָּֽן

verses.restored: In YHWH Divine of Israel he trusted; after him there was none like him among all kings of Judah, nor among those before him.

familiar.text: He trusted in the LORD God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor any that were before him.

modern.text: Hezekiah trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. No king of Judah was like him, either before him or after him.

original.text: בַּיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּטָ֑ח וְאַחֲרָ֞יו לֹא הָיָ֣ה כָמֹ֗הוּ בְּכֹל֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו

verses.restored: He clung to YHWH and did not turn from following him, but kept commandments YHWH commanded Moses.

familiar.text: For he clave to the LORD, and departed not from following him, but kept his commandments, which the LORD commanded Moses.

modern.text: He remained faithful to the LORD and did not turn from following Him; he kept the commandments that the LORD had given Moses.

original.text: וַיִּדְבַּק֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה לֹא סָ֖ר מֵאַֽחֲרָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁמֹר֙ מִצְוֺתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת מֹשֶֽׁה

verses.restored: YHWH was with him; wherever he went he acted wisely/prospered. He rebelled against king of Assyria and did not serve him.

familiar.text: And the LORD was with him; and he prospered whithersoever he went forth: and he rebelled against the king of Assyria, and served him not.

modern.text: And the LORD was with Hezekiah, and he prospered wherever he went. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him.

original.text: וְהָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵ֖א יַשְׂכִּ֑יל וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד בְּמֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר וְלֹ֥א עֲבָדֽוֹ

verses.restored: He struck Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders, from watchtower to fortified city.

familiar.text: He smote the Philistines, even unto Gaza, and the borders thereof, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.

modern.text: He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders, from watchtower to fortified city.

original.text: הֽוּא הִכָּ֧ה אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֛ים עַד עַזָּ֖ה וְאֶת גְּבוּלֶ֑יהָ מִמִּגְדַּ֥ל נוֹצְרִ֖ים עַד עִ֥יר מִבְצָֽר

verses.restored: In fourth year of king Hezekiah, seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria went up against Samaria and besieged it.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria, and besieged it.

modern.text: In the fourth year of Hezekiah’s reign, which was the seventh year of the reign of Hoshea son of Elah over Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against Samaria and besieged it.

original.text: וַֽיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הָֽרְבִיעִית֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ הִ֚יא הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ית לְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עָלָ֞ה שַׁלְמַנְאֶ֧סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֛וּר עַל שֹׁמְר֖וֹן וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: At end of three years they captured it. In sixth year of Hezekiah, ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.

familiar.text: And at the end of three years they took it: even in the sixth year of Hezekiah, that is the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.

modern.text: And at the end of three years, the Assyrians captured it. So Samaria was captured in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel.

original.text: וַֽיִּלְכְּדֻ֗הָ מִקְצֵה֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים בִּשְׁנַת שֵׁ֖שׁ לְחִזְקִיָּ֑ה הִ֣יא שְׁנַת תֵּ֗שַׁע לְהוֹשֵׁ֨עַ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נִלְכְּדָ֖ה שֹׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: King of Assyria exiled Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, Habor by river Gozan, and cities of Medes.

familiar.text: And the king of Assyria did carry away Israel unto Assyria, and put them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes:

modern.text: The king of Assyria exiled the Israelites to Assyria and settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

original.text: וַיֶּ֧גֶל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַשּׁ֑וּרָה וַיַּנְחֵ֞ם בַּחְלַ֧ח וּבְחָב֛וֹר נְהַ֥ר גּוֹזָ֖ן וְעָרֵ֥י מָדָֽי

verses.restored: Because they did not listen to voice of YHWH their Divine but transgressed his covenant—all Moses servant of YHWH commanded—they neither listened nor did.

familiar.text: Because they obeyed not the voice of the LORD their God, but transgressed his covenant, and all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded, and would not hear them, nor do them.

modern.text: This happened because they did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God, but violated His covenant—all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded—and would neither listen nor obey. Sennacherib Invades Judah (2 Chronicles 32:1–8; Psalms 46:1–11)

original.text: עַ֣ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא שָׁמְע֗וּ בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּעַבְרוּ֙ אֶת בְּרִית֔וֹ אֵ֚ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה עֶ֣בֶד יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א עָשֽׂוּ

verses.restored: In fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria went up against all fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

familiar.text: Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah did Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fenced cities of Judah, and took them.

modern.text: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.

original.text: וּבְאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֗ה עָלָ֞ה סַנְחֵרִ֤יב מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ עַ֣ל כָּל עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה הַבְּצֻר֖וֹת וַֽיִּתְפְּשֵֽׂם

verses.restored: Hezekiah king of Judah sent to king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, I have sinned; turn from me. Whatever you place upon me I will bear. King of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

familiar.text: And Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria to Lachish, saying, I have offended; return from me: that which thou puttest on me will I bear. And the king of Assyria appointed unto Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

modern.text: So Hezekiah king of Judah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have done wrong; withdraw from me, and I will pay whatever you demand from me.” And the king of Assyria exacted from Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח חִזְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֣ה אֶל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֩ לָכִ֨ישָׁה לֵאמֹ֤ר חָטָ֨אתִי֙ שׁ֣וּב מֵֽעָלַ֔י אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר תִּתֵּ֥ן עָלַ֖י אֶשָּׂ֑א וַיָּ֨שֶׂם מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֜וּר עַל חִזְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ כִּכַּר כֶּ֔סֶף וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים כִּכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב

verses.restored: Hezekiah gave all silver found in house of YHWH and treasuries of king's house.

familiar.text: And Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasures of the king’s house.

modern.text: Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּן֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔ה אֶת כָּל הַכֶּ֖סֶף הַנִּמְצָ֣א בֵית יְהוָ֑ה וּבְאֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: At that time Hezekiah cut gold from doors of temple of YHWH and doorposts Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave it to king of Assyria.

familiar.text: At that time did Hezekiah cut off the gold from the doors of the temple of the LORD, and from the pillars which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave it to the king of Assyria.

modern.text: At that time Hezekiah stripped the gold with which he had plated the doors and doorposts of the temple of the LORD, and he gave it to the king of Assyria. Sennacherib Threatens Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 32:9–19; Isaiah 36:1–22)

original.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא קִצַּ֨ץ חִזְקִיָּ֜ה אֶת דַּלְת֨וֹת הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וְאֶת הָאֹ֣מְנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִפָּ֔ה חִזְקִיָּ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר

verses.restored: King of Assyria sent Tartan, Rab-saris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a heavy force against Jerusalem. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood by conduit of upper pool on highway of Fuller's Field.

familiar.text: And the king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a great host against Jerusalem. And they went up and came to Jerusalem. And when they were come up, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the fuller’s field.

modern.text: Nevertheless, the king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rabsaris, and the Rabshakeh, along with a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. They advanced up to Jerusalem and stationed themselves by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֡וּר אֶת תַּרְתָּ֥ן וְאֶת רַב סָרִ֣יס וְאֶת רַב שָׁקֵ֨ה מִן לָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּחֵ֥יל כָּבֵ֖ד יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיַּעֲל֣וּ וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ בִּתְעָלַת֙ הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הָֽעֶלְיוֹנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֕ר בִּמְסִלַּ֖ת שְׂדֵ֥ה כוֹבֵֽס

verses.restored: They called to king, and Eliakim son of Hilkiah over house, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder went out to them.

familiar.text: And when they had called to the king, there came out to them Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, which was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder.

modern.text: Then they called for the king; and Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebnah the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to them.

original.text: וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֵּצֵ֧א אֲלֵהֶ֛ם אֶלְיָקִ֥ים בֶּן חִלְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַבָּ֑יִת וְשֶׁבְנָה֙ הַסֹּפֵ֔ר וְיוֹאָ֥ח בֶּן אָסָ֖ף הַמַּזְכִּֽיר

verses.restored: Rabshakeh said to them, Say now to Hezekiah, Thus says great king, king of Assyria: What is this trust in which you trust?

familiar.text: And Rabshakeh said unto them, Speak ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?

modern.text: The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah that this is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours?

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה אִמְרוּ נָ֖א אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר מָ֧ה הַבִּטָּח֛וֹן הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּטָֽחְתָּ

verses.restored: You say, Only a word of lips is counsel and strength for war. Now upon whom do you trust that you rebel against me?

familiar.text: Thou sayest, (but they are but vain words,) I have counsel and strength for the war. Now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebellest against me?

modern.text: You claim to have a strategy and strength for war, but these are empty words. In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?

original.text: אָמַ֨רְתָּ֙ אַךְ דְּבַר שְׂפָתַ֔יִם עֵצָ֥ה וּגְבוּרָ֖ה לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ עַל מִ֣י בָטַ֔חְתָּ כִּ֥י מָרַ֖דְתָּ בִּֽי

verses.restored: Now look, you trust in staff of this crushed reed, Egypt, which if a man leans upon it enters his palm and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

familiar.text: Now, behold, thou trustest upon the staff of this bruised reed, even upon Egypt, on which if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt unto all that trust on him.

modern.text: Look now, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

original.text: עַתָּ֡ה הִנֵּ֣ה בָטַ֣חְתָּ לְּךָ֡ עַל מִשְׁעֶנֶת֩ הַקָּנֶ֨ה הָרָצ֤וּץ הַזֶּה֙ עַל מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִסָּמֵ֥ךְ אִישׁ֙ עָלָ֔יו וּבָ֥א בְכַפּ֖וֹ וּנְקָבָ֑הּ כֵּ֚ן פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לְכָֽל הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: But if you say to me, In YHWH our Divine we trust—is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, Before this altar in Jerusalem you shall bow?

familiar.text: But if ye say unto me, We trust in the LORD our God: is not that he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and hath said to Judah and Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem?

modern.text: But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem: ‘You must worship before this altar in Jerusalem’?

original.text: וְכִי תֹאמְר֣וּן אֵלַ֔י אֶל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ בָּטָ֑חְנוּ הֲלוֹא ה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵסִ֤יר חִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ אֶת בָּמֹתָ֣יו וְאֶת מִזְבְּחֹתָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִפְנֵי֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ הַזֶּ֔ה תִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Now please make a wager with my lord king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able to give riders for them.

familiar.text: Now therefore, I pray thee, give pledges to my lord the king of Assyria, and I will deliver thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.

modern.text: Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ הִתְעָ֣רֶב נָ֔א אֶת אֲדֹנִ֖י אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לְךָ֙ אַלְפַּ֣יִם סוּסִ֔ים אִם תּוּכַ֕ל לָ֥תֶת לְךָ֖ רֹכְבִ֥ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: How then can you turn back face of one governor among least servants of my lord, while you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

familiar.text: How then wilt thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

modern.text: For how can you repel a single officer among the least of my master’s servants when you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

original.text: וְאֵ֣יךְ תָּשִׁ֗יב אֵ֠ת פְּנֵ֨י פַחַ֥ת אַחַ֛ד עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י הַקְּטַנִּ֑ים וַתִּבְטַ֤ח לְךָ֙ עַל מִצְרַ֔יִם לְרֶ֖כֶב וּלְפָרָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: Now have I gone up apart from YHWH against this place to destroy it? YHWH said to me, Go up against this land and destroy it.

familiar.text: Am I now come up without the LORD against this place to destroy it? The LORD said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

modern.text: So now, was it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this place to destroy it? The LORD Himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’”

original.text: עַתָּה֙ הֲמִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עָלִ֛יתִי עַל הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לְהַשְׁחִת֑וֹ יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י עֲלֵ֛ה עַל הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְהַשְׁחִיתָֽהּ

verses.restored: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand; do not speak with us in Judean in ears of people upon wall.

familiar.text: Then said Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, and Shebna, and Joah, unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, to thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand it: and talk not with us in the Jews’ language in the ears of the people that are on the wall.

modern.text: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, along with Shebnah and Joah, said to the Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Do not speak with us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן חִ֠לְקִיָּהוּ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨ה וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה דַּבֶּר נָ֤א אֶל עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲרָמִ֔ית כִּ֥י שֹׁמְעִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְאַל תְּדַבֵּ֤ר עִמָּ֨נוּ֙ יְהוּדִ֔ית בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל הַחֹמָֽה

verses.restored: Rabshakeh said to them, Has my lord sent me to your lord and to you to speak these words? Is it not to men sitting upon wall, who will eat their own excrement and drink their own urine with you?

familiar.text: But Rabshakeh said unto them, Hath my master sent me to thy master, and to thee, to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men which sit on the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?

modern.text: But the Rabshakeh replied, “Has my master sent me to speak these words only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are destined with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה הַעַ֨ל אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ וְאֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲדֹנִ֔י לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲלֹ֣א עַל הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ עַל הַ֣חֹמָ֔ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת חריהם וְלִשְׁתּ֛וֹת אֶת שיניהם עִמָּכֶֽם

verses.restored: Rabshakeh stood and called with great voice in Judean, spoke and said, Hear word of great king, king of Assyria.

familiar.text: Then Rabshakeh stood and cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and spake, saying, Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria:

modern.text: Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebrew: “Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!

original.text: וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל גָּד֖וֹל יְהוּדִ֑ית וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר וַיֹּ֔אמֶר שִׁמְע֛וּ דְּבַר הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הַגָּד֖וֹל מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר

verses.restored: Thus says king: Let Hezekiah not deceive you, for he is not able to deliver you from his hand.

familiar.text: Thus saith the king, Let not Hezekiah deceive you: for he shall not be able to deliver you out of his hand:

modern.text: This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you; he cannot deliver you from my hand.

original.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אַל יַשִּׁ֥יא לָכֶ֖ם חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּי לֹ֣א יוּכַ֔ל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדֽוֹ

verses.restored: Let Hezekiah not make you trust in YHWH, saying, Delivering, YHWH will deliver us, and this city shall not be given into hand of king of Assyria.

familiar.text: Neither let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, The LORD will surely deliver us, and this city shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.

modern.text: Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD when he says, ‘The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’

original.text: וְאַל יַבְטַ֨ח אֶתְכֶ֤ם חִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ אֶל יְהוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר הַצֵּ֥ל יַצִּילֵ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ אֶת הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר

verses.restored: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says king of Assyria: Make blessing/treaty with me and come out to me, and each shall eat from his vine and fig tree and drink water of his cistern,

familiar.text: Hearken not to Hezekiah: for thus saith the king of Assyria, Make an agreement with me by a present, and come out to me, and then eat ye every man of his own vine, and every one of his fig tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his cistern:

modern.text: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink water from his own cistern,

original.text: אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר עֲשֽׂוּ אִתִּ֤י בְרָכָה֙ וּצְא֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְאִכְל֤וּ אִישׁ גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּאֵֽנָת֔וֹ וּשְׁת֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מֵֽי בוֹרֽוֹ

verses.restored: until I come and take you to a land like your land, a land of grain and new wine, bread and vineyards, olive oil and honey, that you may live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah when he entices you, saying, YHWH will deliver us.

familiar.text: Until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of oil olive and of honey, that ye may live, and not die: and hearken not unto Hezekiah, when he persuadeth you, saying, The LORD will deliver us.

modern.text: until I come and take you away to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey—so that you may live and not die. But do not listen to Hezekiah, for he misleads you when he says, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’

original.text: עַד בֹּאִי֩ וְלָקַחְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֜ם אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ כְּאַרְצְכֶ֗ם אֶרֶץ֩ דָּגָ֨ן וְתִיר֜וֹשׁ אֶ֧רֶץ לֶ֣חֶם וּכְרָמִ֗ים אֶ֣רֶץ זֵ֤ית יִצְהָר֙ וּדְבַ֔שׁ וִֽחְי֖וּ וְלֹ֣א תָמֻ֑תוּ וְאַֽל תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּֽי יַסִּ֤ית אֶתְכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֖ה יַצִּילֵֽנוּ

verses.restored: Have gods of nations delivered, each his land, from hand of king of Assyria?

familiar.text: Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered at all his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

modern.text: Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?

original.text: הַהַצֵּ֥ל הִצִּ֛ילוּ אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶת אַרְצ֑וֹ מִיַּ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר

verses.restored: Where are gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they deliver Samaria from my hand?

familiar.text: Where are the gods of Hamath, and of Arpad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? have they delivered Samaria out of mine hand?

modern.text: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?

original.text: אַיֵּה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י חֲמָ֜ת וְאַרְפָּ֗ד אַיֵּ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י סְפַרְוַ֖יִם הֵנַ֣ע וְעִוָּ֑ה כִּֽי הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת שֹׁמְר֖וֹן מִיָּדִֽי

verses.restored: Who among all gods of lands delivered their land from my hand, that YHWH should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?

familiar.text: Who are they among all the gods of the countries, that have delivered their country out of mine hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of mine hand?

modern.text: Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand? How then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”

original.text: מִ֚י בְּכָל אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽאֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִ֑י כִּי יַצִּ֧יל יְהוָ֛ה אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי

verses.restored: People were silent and did not answer him a word, for command of king was, saying, Do not answer him.

familiar.text: But the people held their peace, and answered him not a word: for the king’s commandment was, saying, Answer him not.

modern.text: But the people remained silent and did not answer a word, for Hezekiah had commanded, “Do not answer him.”

original.text: וְהֶחֱרִ֣ישׁוּ הָעָ֔ם וְלֹֽא עָנ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ דָּבָ֑ר כִּי מִצְוַ֨ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הִ֛יא לֵאמֹ֖ר לֹ֥א תַעֲנֻֽהוּ

verses.restored: Eliakim son of Hilkiah over house, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with garments torn and told him words of Rabshakeh.

familiar.text: Then came Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, which was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder, to Hezekiah with their clothes rent, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.

modern.text: Then Hilkiah’s son Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Asaph’s son Joah the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they relayed to him the words of the Rabshakeh.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן חִלְקִיָּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר עַל הַ֠בַּיִת וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א הַסֹּפֵ֜ר וְיוֹאָ֨ח בֶּן אָסָ֧ף הַמַּזְכִּ֛יר אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ דִּבְרֵ֖י רַב שָׁקֵֽה

translation_notes: Hezekiah's reform includes destruction of local shrines and a revered bronze object. Reform may challenge exploitative institutions, but this text cannot authorize attacks on living religious communities or cultural heritage.
The bronze serpent is reduced to 'a bronze thing' because an old liberation symbol has become an object of cult. The critique concerns how symbols function, not a blanket ban on sacred art.
Hezekiah's campaign against Philistine cities and rebellion against Assyria remain military and imperial actions; positive royal evaluation does not erase conquered civilians.
The recap of Samaria's fall uses covenant theology but must preserve Assyria's siege and deportation as imperial violence.
Sennacherib captures Judah's fortified cities before Jerusalem's crisis. The displaced, killed, taxed, and besieged population extends far beyond the capital narrative.
Hezekiah strips temple doors and treasury to pay tribute. Sacred wealth cannot guarantee security, and rulers may transfer communal resources under coercion.
Rabshakeh uses accurate critique, exaggeration, humiliation, religious claims, bodily terror, economic promise, and public-language strategy as siege propaganda.
The threat of eating excrement and drinking urine describes siege starvation and is intended to terrify civilians. It must not be sensationalized or used as degrading humor.
Assyria's promise of vines, cisterns, and a similar land disguises forced deportation as benevolent relocation.
Rabshakeh claims YHWH authorized the invasion. Claims of Divine military permission require moral scrutiny and may never be treated as self-authenticating.
The people's silence is disciplined crisis response under royal command, not consent or proof that they were unafraid.
safety_note: Do not use Hezekiah's reform to justify religious vandalism, erase Philistine civilians, blame Samarian exiles, celebrate temple stripping, or imitate siege propaganda. Center civilians hearing threats in their own language, communities already conquered, and the difference between promised relocation and forced deportation.
